title: 计算机科学，从零搭建 · 第39部分：分布式系统（二）：规模

chapters.Frontier: 9. 前沿：协调能少到什么程度？
chapters.Outro: 回顾、习题，以及它们会在哪里再出现

db8d059002ec.en: The thirty novels, cut into forty-eight pieces and spread across sixteen Pebbles. Each Pebble counts the words in its pieces, the counts are shuffled so that every word goes to one place, and sixteen merges produce the answer: MapReduce, the way Google counted the web in 2004. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is every task, on every machine, over time: maps in blue, then reduces in purple. <bookmark mark='b'/> At four tenths of a second, Pebble four dies. The task it was running is lost, and so are the outputs of the maps it had already finished, because they lived on its own disk. The master hands all of that work to the others. <bookmark mark='c'/> Near the end, idle machines run backup copies of the last slow tasks, and whichever copy finishes first wins. <bookmark mark='d'/> Six tenths of a second, against two point seven on one Pebble, with a machine lost along the way, and the twenty words and their counts identical to the one-machine Job's.
db8d059002ec.zh: 三十部小说被切成四十八块，分散到十六台 Pebble 上。每台 Pebble 统计自己那几块里的词，计数经过洗牌（shuffle），让每个词都汇集到同一个地方，再由十六次合并得出答案：这就是 MapReduce，2004年 Google 统计整个万维网的方法。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里是每一台机器上的每一个任务随时间的分布：map 是蓝色，随后的 reduce 是紫色。<bookmark mark='b'/>在零点四秒时，四号 Pebble 宕掉了。它正在运行的任务丢失了，它已经完成的那些 map 的输出也丢失了，因为它们存放在它自己的磁盘上。主节点把这些工作全部交给其余的机器。<bookmark mark='c'/>接近尾声时，空闲的机器为最后几个慢任务运行备份副本，哪一份先完成，就算哪一份。<bookmark mark='d'/>零点六秒，对比单台 Pebble 上的二点七秒，途中还丢了一台机器，而那二十个词和它们的计数，与单机运行 那项任务的结果完全相同。

31deeaaf7b81.en: This is Part 39 of Computer Science, Built: Distributed systems at scale. <bookmark mark='a'/> At the scale of a datacenter, every guarantee has a price in latency or availability. We measure what replication costs and how stale its reads are, state the CAP theorem precisely and build data types that cannot conflict. We spread data with consistent hashing, commit across machines with two-phase commit and with Spanner's atomic clocks, run the Job as MapReduce, and watch one slow server in a hundred make most requests slow. Part 38 asked whether machines can agree at all. This part asks what agreement costs when there are thousands of machines, some always failing, and an ocean between them, and how much of it we can do without. Almost every system you use, from a search box to a shopping cart, is an answer to that question, and each answer is a choice about which anomalies its users are allowed to see. By the end we will have measured those choices, not just named them, and Act Seven will be complete.
31deeaaf7b81.zh: 这是计算机科学，从零搭建，第39部分：大规模分布式系统。<bookmark mark='a'/>在数据中心的规模上，每一项保证都要以延迟或可用性为代价。我们会测量复制的成本，以及它的读取有多陈旧；准确地表述 CAP 定理；并构造不可能发生冲突的数据类型。我们用一致性哈希来分散数据，用两阶段提交、以及 Spanner 的原子钟，跨机器提交事务；把 那项任务作为 MapReduce 来运行；还会看到，一百台服务器里只要有一台慢，就会让大多数请求变慢。第38部分问的是：机器究竟能不能达成一致。这一部分问的是：当机器有成千上万台、其中总有一些在出故障、彼此之间还隔着一片大洋时，一致要付出什么代价，以及其中有多少是我们可以不要的。你用的几乎每一个系统，从搜索框到购物车，都是对这个问题的一种回答，而每一种回答，都是在选择允许用户看到哪些异常。到最后，我们会把这些选择测量出来，而不只是给它们起个名字，第七幕也将就此完成。

289cd3b2a087.en: Chapter one. The datacenter, and replication.
289cd3b2a087.zh: 第一章。数据中心，以及复制。

1fd9f35e5246.en: Luiz Barroso and Urs Hölzle called the modern datacenter a single computer: tens of thousands of servers, one program. Its distances are what shape everything in this part. Stretch time so that one processor cycle takes a second. <bookmark mark='a'/> Then a cache hit is three seconds and main memory five minutes. A round trip to another machine in the same building is seventeen days; reading a random spot on a solid-state disk, three and a half; a spinning disk's seek, a year. A round trip from California to Europe takes fifteen years, and a TCP retransmission timeout a century. <bookmark mark='b'/> So every protocol here is judged in round trips, and every clever idea is a way to make fewer of them.
1fd9f35e5246.zh: Luiz Barroso 和 Urs Hölzle 把现代数据中心称作一台计算机：数以万计的服务器，运行一个程序。正是它内部的种种距离，塑造了这一部分里的一切。把时间拉长，让一个处理器周期等于一秒。<bookmark mark='a'/>那么一次缓存命中是三秒，访问主存是五分钟。到同一栋楼里另一台机器的一次往返是十七天；随机读取固态硬盘上的一个位置，三天半；机械硬盘的一次寻道，一年。从加州到欧洲的一次往返要十五年，而一次 TCP 重传超时，是一个世纪。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以，这里的每一个协议都以往返次数来衡量，而每一个巧妙的想法，都是为了减少往返。

0acdf0df4605.en: Data is copied for three reasons: to survive failures, to serve more reads, and to be near users. There are three basic ways. <bookmark mark='a'/> A single leader takes every write and streams its log to followers, as PostgreSQL and MySQL do, and as Raft does. <bookmark mark='b'/> Several leaders, one per datacenter, let every region write locally, at the price of conflicts when two leaders accept different writes to the same thing. <bookmark mark='c'/> Or no leader at all: clients write to several replicas and read from several, and correctness comes from counting, as in Amazon's Dynamo. <bookmark mark='d'/> Independently, the leader can wait for followers before acknowledging a write, which is durable but slow and stalls if one follower dies, or not wait, which is fast, but leaves the followers behind.
0acdf0df4605.zh: 复制数据有三个理由：在故障中存活，承担更多的读取，以及靠近用户。基本的做法有三种。<bookmark mark='a'/>单一领导者接收所有写入，并把它的日志以流的方式发送给跟随者，PostgreSQL 和 MySQL 是这样做的，Raft 也是。<bookmark mark='b'/>多个领导者，每个数据中心一个，让每个地区都能在本地写入，代价是：当两个领导者对同一样东西接受了不同的写入时，就会发生冲突。<bookmark mark='c'/>或者干脆没有领导者：客户端写入若干个副本，也从若干个副本读取，正确性来自计数，就像 Amazon 的 Dynamo 那样。<bookmark mark='d'/>另外，与此无关的一个选择是：领导者可以先等跟随者，再确认一次写入，这样数据持久，但速度慢，而且只要有一个跟随者宕掉就会卡住；也可以不等，这样很快，但会让跟随者落在后面。

0f5b61fd2ce7.en: Asynchronous followers lag, and users notice. Here is one leader and two followers that apply each write a hundred milliseconds late on average, and a user who posts something and immediately reloads the page, with the read sent to any replica. <bookmark mark='a'/> Two thirds of the time, the post is missing: the read went to a follower that has not seen it yet. After two hundred milliseconds, still nine percent. <bookmark mark='b'/> The usual remedies are small and specific: read your own data from the leader, or remember the position of your last write and wait for a replica that has reached it, and always read from the same replica, so that time never seems to run backwards.
0f5b61fd2ce7.zh: 异步的跟随者会滞后，而用户会察觉到。这里有一个领导者和两个跟随者，跟随者平均晚一百毫秒应用每一次写入；还有一个用户，发了一条帖子，随即刷新页面，而这次读取被发往任意一个副本。<bookmark mark='a'/>三分之二的情况下，帖子不见了：读取落到了一个还没看到它的跟随者上。过了两百毫秒，仍然有百分之九。<bookmark mark='b'/>常用的补救办法既小又具体：从领导者读取你自己的数据；或者记住你上一次写入的位置，等待一个已经追上这个位置的副本；并且总是从同一个副本读取，这样时间就永远不会看起来在倒流。

34a73bc09315.en: With more than one leader, two regions can accept writes to the same key at the same moment. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here Europe sets a shopping cart to a book while the US sets it to a pen; each write takes fifty milliseconds to cross, so neither saw the other. They are concurrent, and something must decide. <bookmark mark='b'/> The simplest rule, last writer wins, keeps the larger timestamp and silently throws the other away. Worse, timestamps come from clocks. <bookmark mark='c'/> If the US clock runs a hundred milliseconds fast, a write from Europe that had already seen the American one can still carry a smaller timestamp, and lose: the newer value is discarded for the older. <bookmark mark='d'/> We simulated a busy key written five times a second from each region. About one write in five is concurrent with another, so last writer wins silently loses one write in ten, and with clock skew beyond the replication delay, inversions add more: almost a quarter of all writes at a quarter of a second of skew. <bookmark mark='e'/> Version vectors, Part 38's vector clocks with one counter per replica, tell the two cases apart exactly. Causally later writes replace earlier ones, and concurrent writes are kept side by side as siblings for the application to merge, as Dynamo and Riak do. Merging them automatically is what the next chapter is about.
34a73bc09315.zh: 有了不止一个领导者，两个地区就可能在同一时刻接受对同一个键的写入。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里，欧洲把购物车设成一本书，而美国把它设成一支笔；每次写入传到对面要五十毫秒，所以双方都没看到对方。它们是并发的，必须由某种机制来裁决。<bookmark mark='b'/>最简单的规则是最后写入者胜：保留时间戳较大的那个，悄无声息地扔掉另一个。更糟的是，时间戳来自时钟。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果美国的时钟快了一百毫秒，那么欧洲的一次写入，即使它已经看到了美国那次写入，也仍可能带着更小的时间戳，于是落败：较新的值被丢弃，留下了较旧的值。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们模拟了一个繁忙的键，每个地区每秒写入五次。大约每五次写入中就有一次与另一次写入并发，所以最后写入者胜会悄悄丢掉十分之一的写入；而当时钟偏差超过复制延迟时，顺序颠倒还会再添上更多：在四分之一秒的偏差下，丢失的写入接近全部写入的四分之一。<bookmark mark='e'/>版本向量，也就是第38部分的向量时钟，每个副本一个计数器，能够精确地区分这两种情况。因果上较晚的写入替换较早的写入，而并发的写入则作为兄弟值并排保留，交给应用程序去合并，Dynamo 和 Riak 就是这样做的。如何自动合并它们，正是下一章要讲的内容。

86166ec86230.zh: 第二章。法定人数与一致性。

740f1404b0d3.en: Leaderless systems count. <bookmark mark='a'/> Write to W of the N replicas, read from R of them, and keep whichever value carries the newest version number. If R plus W is greater than N, every set of replicas you read overlaps every set that was written, so at least one replica you read has the latest write: the majorities of Paxos, generalized. <bookmark mark='b'/> Amazon's Dynamo, in 2007, typically used three replicas, writing and reading two. For speed you can write and read one, and accept that reads may be stale. <bookmark mark='c'/> And when a home replica is unreachable, Dynamo writes to some other machine that hands the data back later, so writes never fail, at the cost that quorums no longer strictly overlap.
740f1404b0d3.zh: 无领导者的系统靠计数。<bookmark mark='a'/>写入 N 个副本中的 W 个，从其中 R 个读取，保留版本号最新的那个值。如果 R 加 W 大于 N，那么你读取的每一组副本，都与被写入的每一组副本有交集，所以你读到的副本中至少有一个持有最新的写入：这就是 Paxos 中多数派的推广。<bookmark mark='b'/>2007年，Amazon 的 Dynamo 通常使用三个副本，写两个、读两个。为了速度，你也可以只写一个、只读一个，并接受读到的可能是陈旧数据。<bookmark mark='c'/>而当本该存放数据的某个副本无法访问时，Dynamo 会写到另一台机器上，由它稍后把数据交还，这样写入永远不会失败，代价是法定人数不再严格地相交。

0d7029025da5.en: Peter Bailis and his colleagues asked how stale non-strict quorums actually are. We simulated it: a write reaches each replica after a random delay averaging ten milliseconds, and a read starts some time after the write was acknowledged. <bookmark mark='a'/> When R plus W exceeds N, no read was ever stale, as the argument says. With three replicas, reading and writing one, a read issued at the instant of acknowledgement misses the write more than half the time; five milliseconds later, a third; fifty milliseconds later, three in a thousand. <bookmark mark='b'/> Eventual consistency is usually very soon, and now we can say how soon.
0d7029025da5.zh: Peter Bailis 和他的同事们问过：非严格的法定人数，到底有多陈旧？我们做了模拟：一次写入经过一段平均十毫秒的随机延迟到达每个副本，而一次读取在写入被确认之后的某个时刻开始。<bookmark mark='a'/>当 R 加 W 大于 N 时，没有一次读取是陈旧的，正如前面的论证所说。三个副本、读写各一个时，在确认那一刻发出的读取，有一半以上会错过这次写入；五毫秒之后，是三分之一；五十毫秒之后，是千分之三。<bookmark mark='b'/>最终一致性通常来得很快，而现在我们能说出有多快。

823f2354028b.en: Sloppy quorums and failed replicas leave copies that disagree, and something must find the differences. Comparing two replicas of a million keys by sending one hash per key costs sixteen megabytes, even when nothing differs. <bookmark mark='a'/> Ralph Merkle's tree of hashes does better. Each leaf hashes a small range of keys, each node hashes its children, and the root summarizes everything. Two replicas compare roots; if they match, they are done. If not, they compare the children, and descend only into the branches whose hashes differ. <bookmark mark='b'/> With ten keys out of a million differing, our replicas exchanged eleven kilobytes in six round trips and found every one. Even with ten thousand differences, the cost stays below a third of the naive one. <bookmark mark='c'/> Dynamo-style stores combine three repairs: read repair fixes stale replicas that a read happens to notice, hinted handoff delivers writes held for a replica that was down, and anti-entropy compares Merkle trees in the background. The same trees check the integrity of Git repositories, of BitTorrent's pieces, and of certificate transparency logs.
823f2354028b.zh: 宽松法定人数和失效的副本，会留下彼此不一致的副本，必须有某种机制把差异找出来。比较两个各有一百万个键的副本，如果每个键发送一个哈希，就要花十六兆字节，哪怕根本没有任何差异。<bookmark mark='a'/>Ralph Merkle 的哈希树做得更好。每个叶子对一小段范围内的键求哈希，每个节点对它的子节点求哈希，而根概括了一切。两个副本先比较根；如果相同，就完事了。如果不同，就比较子节点，并且只深入哈希不同的那些分支。<bookmark mark='b'/>在一百万个键里有十个不同时，我们的副本交换了十一千字节，用了六次往返，把每一处差异都找了出来。即使有一万处差异，成本仍低于朴素做法的三分之一。<bookmark mark='c'/>Dynamo 风格的存储结合了三种修复：读修复，修好读取时恰好发现的陈旧副本；提示移交，把为宕机副本暂存的写入交付给它；反熵，则在后台比较 Merkle 树。同样的树还用来校验 Git 仓库、BitTorrent 的数据块，以及证书透明度日志的完整性。

8fe2368e2654.en: What should a read return? There is a ladder of answers. <bookmark mark='a'/> At the top, linearizability, from Part 33: the system behaves like a single copy, and every operation takes effect at one instant between its start and its end. Sequential consistency keeps a single order but loosens its tie to real time. Causal consistency promises only that you never see an effect before its cause. Session guarantees are promises to one user, like reading your own writes. And eventual consistency promises only that if writes stop, the replicas converge. <bookmark mark='b'/> Each step down needs less coordination. Linearizability needs a round trip to a majority for every operation; causal consistency can be served by any replica that has seen the causes.
8fe2368e2654.zh: 一次读取应该返回什么？答案排成一架梯子。<bookmark mark='a'/>最顶端是可线性化，来自第33部分：系统表现得就像只有一份副本，每个操作都在它开始和结束之间的某一个瞬间生效。顺序一致性保留单一的顺序，但放松了它与真实时间的联系。因果一致性只承诺：你永远不会在看到原因之前看到结果。会话保证是对单个用户的承诺，比如能读到自己写入的数据。而最终一致性只承诺：如果写入停止，副本终将收敛。<bookmark mark='b'/>每往下走一级，需要的协调就少一些。可线性化的每个操作都需要与多数派往返一次；而因果一致性，可以由任何一个已经看到了那些原因的副本来提供。

05f9e123c7ea.en: Eric Brewer conjectured in 2000, and Seth Gilbert and Nancy Lynch proved in 2002, the CAP theorem. <bookmark mark='a'/> No system can be both linearizable and available, meaning every request to a live replica gets an answer, in a network that can partition. <bookmark mark='b'/> The proof is two lines. Cut replica A off from replica B. A client writes at A, and availability forces A to accept. Another reads at B, and availability forces B to answer, without being able to hear from A, so it returns the old value. <bookmark mark='c'/> So during a partition, a system either refuses the side without a majority, as Raft did in the last part, or answers everyone and sorts out the conflicting writes afterwards. <bookmark mark='d'/> Daniel Abadi pointed out that the more important choice is the everyday one: partitions are rare, but round trips are constant, so even without partitions every system trades latency against consistency.
05f9e123c7ea.zh: Eric Brewer 在2000年提出猜想，Seth Gilbert 和 Nancy Lynch 在2002年给出证明：这就是 CAP 定理。<bookmark mark='a'/>在一个可能发生分区的网络中，没有任何系统能同时做到可线性化和可用，这里的可用，是指发往存活副本的每个请求都能得到回答。<bookmark mark='b'/>证明只有两行。把副本 A 和副本 B 隔开。一个客户端在 A 上写入，可用性迫使 A 接受。另一个客户端在 B 上读取，可用性迫使 B 作答，而它无法从 A 那里得到消息，于是返回旧值。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以在分区期间，一个系统要么拒绝没有多数派的那一边，就像上一部分里 Raft 所做的那样；要么回答所有人，事后再去整理相互冲突的写入。<bookmark mark='d'/>Daniel Abadi 指出，更重要的是日常的那个选择：分区很少见，但往返无时不在，所以即使没有分区，每个系统也都在延迟与一致性之间做权衡。

abea2d3f17f1.en: Chapter three. Conflict-free replicated data types.
abea2d3f17f1.zh: 第三章。无冲突复制数据类型。

aebfffa73d89.en: Multi-leader and leaderless systems must merge conflicting copies. In 2011 Marc Shapiro and his colleagues found a way to make every merge safe: design the data type so that merging is a join. <bookmark mark='a'/> Merging must be commutative, so the order of messages does not matter; associative, so the grouping does not matter; and idempotent, so receiving the same state twice does nothing. <bookmark mark='b'/> Mathematically, the states form a join-semilattice: updates only move up, and merge takes the least upper bound. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then convergence is a theorem: if every update eventually reaches every replica, in any order and any number of times, all replicas end in the same state. <bookmark mark='d'/> The proof is that a replica's state is just the join of the updates it has seen, and the three laws let us reorder, regroup and deduplicate them freely.
aebfffa73d89.zh: 多领导者和无领导者的系统，必须合并相互冲突的副本。2011年，Marc Shapiro 和他的同事们找到了一种让每一次合并都安全的方法：把数据类型设计成，合并就是求并（join）。<bookmark mark='a'/>合并必须满足交换律，这样消息的顺序无关紧要；满足结合律，这样分组的方式无关紧要；还要满足幂等律，这样同一个状态收到两次，也不会有任何变化。<bookmark mark='b'/>从数学上说，这些状态构成一个并半格：更新只会向上走，而合并取最小上界。<bookmark mark='c'/>于是收敛就成了一条定理：只要每个更新最终都到达每个副本，无论顺序如何、无论到达多少次，所有副本最后都处于同一个状态。<bookmark mark='d'/>证明是：一个副本的状态，不过是它见过的所有更新的并，而那三条定律让我们可以随意地重新排序、重新分组和去重。

63b532f71858.en: The simplest example is a counter. A naive replicated counter, add the other replica's count when you merge, double-counts the moment a merge is repeated. <bookmark mark='a'/> A grow-only counter keeps one slot per replica. Each replica increments only its own slot, merging takes the maximum of each slot, and the value is the sum. Here replica A adds two and B adds one; C merges A; A merges B; then they gossip in no particular order. <bookmark mark='b'/> Every replica ends with two, one, zero: a value of three, though messages crossed and some states were merged twice. <bookmark mark='c'/> Two of them make a counter that can go down, and a last-writer-wins register keeps whichever value has the highest timestamp, which is a join too, though it silently discards the losing write.
63b532f71858.zh: 最简单的例子是计数器。一个朴素的复制计数器，合并时把另一个副本的计数加进来，一旦某次合并被重复，就会重复计数。<bookmark mark='a'/>只增计数器为每个副本保留一个槽位。每个副本只递增自己的槽位，合并时对每个槽位取最大值，而计数值就是所有槽位之和。这里，副本 A 加二，B 加一；C 合并 A；A 合并 B；然后它们不按任何特定顺序，以 gossip 的方式互相传播。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个副本最后都是二、一、零：值为三，尽管消息交错而过，有些状态还被合并了两次。<bookmark mark='c'/>两个这样的计数器能组成一个可以减少的计数器；而最后写入者胜寄存器保留时间戳最高的那个值，这同样是一种并，尽管它会悄无声息地丢弃落败的那次写入。

22c79400fc00.en: We tested four CRDTs against a naive alternative, a thousand runs each: four replicas, forty random operations, merges between random pairs in random directions, and finally gossip until every pair has merged. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every CRDT converged in every run. The naive set, which merges by replaying the other replica's log of adds and removes, ended with every replica agreeing in only fifteen runs of a thousand, because adding and removing the same element do not commute.
22c79400fc00.zh: 我们拿四种 CRDT 和一个朴素的替代方案做了测试，每种跑一千次：四个副本，四十个随机操作，在随机的副本对之间、沿随机的方向合并，最后再以 gossip 传播，直到每一对副本都合并过。<bookmark mark='a'/>每一种 CRDT 在每一次运行中都收敛了。而那个朴素的集合，合并时重放另一个副本的添加与删除日志，在一千次运行中，只有十五次最后所有副本达成一致，因为对同一个元素的添加和删除是不可交换的。

b56971c46c61.en: The same idea scales to richer types. <bookmark mark='a'/> An observed-remove set tags every addition uniquely, and a removal deletes only the tags it has seen, so an addition concurrent with a removal survives. <bookmark mark='b'/> Sequence CRDTs give every character an identifier that sorts between its neighbours', so two people typing at the same spot see their characters interleaved the same way on every replica: the basis of collaborative editors that work offline. <bookmark mark='c'/> Google Docs took the other road, operational transformation, rewriting concurrent edits against each other through a central server. <bookmark mark='d'/> The catch: a CRDT guarantees that replicas agree, not that they agree on what users intended, and an invariant spanning replicas, like a balance that must not go negative, still needs coordination.
b56971c46c61.zh: 同样的思想可以推广到更丰富的类型。<bookmark mark='a'/>观察删除集合给每一次添加打上唯一的标签，而一次删除只删去它见过的那些标签，所以与删除并发的添加会保留下来。<bookmark mark='b'/>序列 CRDT 给每个字符一个标识符，它在排序上位于左右两个邻居的标识符之间，于是两个人在同一个位置打字时，他们的字符在每个副本上都以同样的方式交错排列：这正是可以离线工作的协同编辑器的基础。<bookmark mark='c'/>Google Docs 走了另一条路，即操作变换：通过一台中心服务器，把并发的编辑相互改写。<bookmark mark='d'/>问题在于：CRDT 保证的是副本之间达成一致，而不是它们在用户的意图上达成一致；而一个跨越多个副本的不变量，比如余额不能为负，仍然需要协调。

a21ddddee0c9.en: Text is the hardest case, because edits name positions, and positions shift. <bookmark mark='a'/> Alice and Bob share the sentence the cat sat. At the same moment Alice types fat in front of cat, and Bob changes sat to ran. <bookmark mark='b'/> If each replica simply replays the other's edits by position, insert at four, delete at eight, Bob ends up right by luck, and Alice's copy deletes the wrong word: the fat ran sat. The replicas disagree for ever. <bookmark mark='c'/> A sequence CRDT such as RGA, the replicated growable array, never uses positions. Every character gets a unique identifier, a counter and the replica's name, and an insertion says which character it follows. Deletions leave an invisible tombstone, and characters inserted after the same one are ordered by identifier. Both replicas now read the fat cat ran. <bookmark mark='d'/> In five hundred random sessions of three editors, RGA converged every time, and positional replay never did. Editors like Automerge and Yjs are built this way.
a21ddddee0c9.zh: 文本是最难的情形，因为编辑指明的是位置，而位置会移动。<bookmark mark='a'/>Alice 和 Bob 共享一句话：the cat sat。在同一时刻，Alice 在 cat 前面输入 fat，Bob 把 sat 改成 ran。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果每个副本只是按位置重放对方的编辑，在第四个位置插入，在第八个位置删除，那么 Bob 碰巧得到了正确的结果，而 Alice 的副本删掉了错误的单词：the fat ran sat。两个副本从此永远不一致。<bookmark mark='c'/>像 RGA，也就是可复制增长数组，这样的序列 CRDT，从不使用位置。每个字符都有一个唯一的标识符，由一个计数器和副本的名字组成，而一次插入指明的是它跟在哪个字符后面。删除会留下一个看不见的墓碑，而跟在同一个字符后面插入的那些字符，按标识符排序。现在两个副本读到的都是 the fat cat ran。<bookmark mark='d'/>在五百次三人编辑的随机会话中，RGA 每次都收敛了，而按位置重放一次也没有收敛。Automerge 和 Yjs 这样的编辑器就是这样构建的。

896572e9d329.en: Convergence is not free. <bookmark mark='a'/> We edited one RGA document twenty thousand times, three edits in ten being deletions. Deleted characters cannot simply vanish, because a late insertion might still refer to them, so they stay as tombstones: after twenty thousand edits, eight thousand visible characters and almost six thousand tombstones. <bookmark mark='b'/> Every element carries its own identifier and its neighbour's, so the document costs forty-two bytes for each character you can see, against one for plain text. <bookmark mark='c'/> A tombstone can be thrown away only when every replica has seen the deletion, and knowing that requires the replicas to coordinate, the very thing CRDTs avoid. <bookmark mark='d'/> Practical libraries such as Automerge and Yjs store runs of consecutive identifiers and compress by column, and cut the overhead by orders of magnitude. Making that efficient was one of the research problems of the last decade.
896572e9d329.zh: 收敛不是免费的。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们把一份 RGA 文档编辑了两万次，其中十分之三的编辑是删除。被删除的字符不能直接消失，因为一次迟到的插入可能还会引用它们，所以它们作为墓碑留了下来：两万次编辑之后，有八千个可见字符，以及将近六千个墓碑。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个元素都携带自己的标识符和邻居的标识符，所以这份文档每个可见字符要花四十二个字节，而纯文本只要一个。<bookmark mark='c'/>只有当每个副本都看到了这次删除，墓碑才能被丢弃，而要知道这一点，副本之间就必须协调，这恰恰是 CRDT 想要避免的事情。<bookmark mark='d'/>实用的库，比如 Automerge 和 Yjs，把连续的标识符存成游程，并按列压缩，把开销降低了几个数量级。让这件事变得高效，是过去十年的研究课题之一。

02e6616b579e.en: With more data than one machine holds, keys must be spread over many. The obvious rule, hash the key and take it modulo the number of machines, has a fatal flaw. <bookmark mark='a'/> Add an eleventh machine to ten, and ninety-one percent of all keys move. In 1997 David Karger and his colleagues, working on what became Akamai, proposed a ring instead. <bookmark mark='b'/> Hash the machines onto a circle, and hash each key onto the same circle; a key belongs to the first machine clockwise from it. <bookmark mark='c'/> A new machine lands somewhere on the circle and takes keys only from its neighbour. Adding the eleventh machine moves eight point six percent of the keys, close to the minimum possible, one eleventh. Jump hashing and rendezvous hashing achieve the same with less memory or simpler code.
02e6616b579e.zh: 当数据多到一台机器放不下时，键就必须分散到许多台机器上。最直观的规则，是对键取哈希，再对机器台数取模，可它有一个致命的缺陷。<bookmark mark='a'/>在十台机器之外再加第十一台，所有键里有百分之九十一都要搬家。1997年，David Karger 和他的同事们在后来成为 Akamai 的那项工作中，提出改用一个环。<bookmark mark='b'/>把机器哈希到一个圆上，再把每个键也哈希到同一个圆上；一个键归属于从它出发、顺时针遇到的第一台机器。<bookmark mark='c'/>新机器落在圆上的某个位置，只从它的邻居那里接过一部分键。加入第十一台机器，只移动百分之八点六的键，接近理论上的最小值，十一分之一。跳跃哈希（jump hashing）和会合哈希（rendezvous hashing）能用更少的内存或更简单的代码做到同样的事。

c5916f70bac5.en: One problem remains. <bookmark mark='a'/> With one point per machine, ten machines cut the circle into very unequal arcs. In our test with a hundred thousand keys, the busiest machine held three point four times its share and the idlest an eighth. <bookmark mark='b'/> So each machine is placed on the circle many times, as virtual nodes. With two hundred and fifty-six points each, the busiest holds sixteen percent more than its share, and the spread keeps falling as one over the square root of the number of points. A machine twice as large simply gets twice as many points.
c5916f70bac5.zh: 还剩一个问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>如果每台机器在圆上只占一个点，十台机器会把圆切成长短悬殊的弧段。在我们用十万个键做的测试里，最忙的机器承担了它应得份额的三点四倍，最闲的只有八分之一。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以每台机器要在圆上放置很多次，作为虚拟节点。每台放两百五十六个点，最忙的机器只比应得份额多出百分之十六，而且这种偏差还会按点数平方根的倒数继续缩小。一台容量大一倍的机器，只需分到多一倍的点。

06e2aa77aa17.en: Even a perfect hash spreads keys evenly, not requests. Real popularity follows Zipf's law: the most popular key gets a large share of all traffic, the second half as much, and so on. <bookmark mark='a'/> We sent two million requests for a million keys to a hundred shards. With uniform popularity, the busiest shard is within four percent of the mean. With Zipf's exponent one, the hottest key alone carries seven percent of all requests, and its shard is almost eight times busier than average; at one point two, twenty times. This is the celebrity problem: one account followed by millions. <bookmark mark='b'/> The remedy is to split the hot key: add a random suffix to every write, so it spreads over twenty sub-keys, and have readers fetch and merge them all. Splitting only the ten hottest keys brings the worst shard, at exponent one, under two times the mean. Caching the key in front of the shards, or replicating it more widely, works for reads. <bookmark mark='c'/> Range partitioning, used by Bigtable, HBase and Spanner, keeps neighbouring keys together so that scans are cheap, but it invites an even worse hot spot: if keys are timestamps, every new write goes to the last range.
06e2aa77aa17.zh: 即使是完美的哈希，均匀分散的也只是键，而不是请求。真实的热度服从齐普夫定律：最热门的键拿走全部流量中的一大份，第二热门的只有它的一半，依此类推。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们向一百个分片发送了两百万个请求，访问一百万个键。如果热度均匀，最忙的分片与平均值相差不到百分之四。当齐普夫指数为一时，最热的那一个键就独占了全部请求的百分之七，它所在的分片比平均水平忙将近八倍；指数为一点二时，是二十倍。这就是名人问题：一个账号被几百万人关注。<bookmark mark='b'/>解决办法是拆分热点键：每次写入都加上一个随机后缀，让它分散到二十个子键上，读的一方则把它们全部取回再合并。只拆分最热的十个键，就能让指数为一时最坏的分片降到平均值的两倍以下。对于读，在分片前面加一层缓存，或者把这个键复制到更多地方，也都管用。<bookmark mark='c'/>范围分区被 Bigtable、HBase 和 Spanner 采用，它把相邻的键放在一起，让扫描变得便宜，却会招来更糟的热点：如果键是时间戳，每一次新的写入都会落到最后一个范围上。

c61f4ea09016.en: Inside one datacenter, a table of who owns which arc fits on every machine. Across millions of peers it does not. In 2001 Ion Stoica and his colleagues built Chord. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each node keeps a small table of fingers: the node responsible for its own identifier plus one, plus two, plus four, and so on, doubling, thirty-two entries in all. <bookmark mark='b'/> To find a key, a node forwards the lookup to its farthest finger that does not pass the key. The distance remaining at least halves with each hop, so a lookup takes at most log n hops. <bookmark mark='c'/> We built rings of sixteen to sixteen thousand nodes: lookups took on average about half of log n, plus one, under eight hops with sixteen thousand nodes. <bookmark mark='d'/> Kademlia measures distance by exclusive-or instead, which is symmetric, and runs BitTorrent's peer discovery to this day.
c61f4ea09016.zh: 在一个数据中心内部，记录谁拥有哪段弧的表可以放在每台机器上。可要是有几百万个对等节点，就放不下了。2001年，Ion Stoica 和他的同事们构建了 Chord。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个节点维护一张很小的指针表（finger table）：记下负责它自己的标识符加一、加二、加四，如此依次翻倍的那些节点，一共三十二项。<bookmark mark='b'/>要查找一个键，节点就把查询转发给不越过这个键的最远那个指针。剩下的距离每跳一次至少减半，所以一次查找最多需要 log n 跳。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们搭建了从十六个到一万六千个节点的环：查找平均大约需要 log n 的一半再加一跳，在一万六千个节点时也不到八跳。<bookmark mark='d'/>Kademlia 则改用异或来度量距离，这种距离是对称的，它至今仍在支撑 BitTorrent 的节点发现。

82141a43bdec.en: A transaction that touches data on several machines must commit everywhere or nowhere. Jim Gray's two-phase commit, from 1978, does it with a coordinator. <bookmark mark='a'/> In phase one the coordinator asks every participant to prepare. Each one makes its part of the transaction durable, holds its locks, and votes. A yes vote is a promise: I will commit if you tell me to, even if I crash and restart. <bookmark mark='b'/> If every vote is yes, the coordinator writes commit to its own log, which is the moment of decision, and tells everyone; any no means abort. <bookmark mark='c'/> Unlike consensus, any single participant can veto the outcome. That is what makes it atomic commitment.
82141a43bdec.zh: 一个事务如果涉及好几台机器上的数据，就必须要么处处提交，要么处处都不提交。Jim Gray 在1978年提出的两阶段提交，靠一个协调者来做到这一点。<bookmark mark='a'/>在第一阶段，协调者请每个参与者做好准备。每个参与者把自己那部分事务持久化，继续持有锁，然后投票。投赞成票就是一个承诺：只要你让我提交，我就提交，哪怕我崩溃后重启也一样。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果所有票都是赞成，协调者就把“提交”写进自己的日志，这一刻就是做出决定的时刻，然后通知所有人；只要有一票反对，就中止。<bookmark mark='c'/>和共识不同，任何一个参与者都可以否决结果。正是这一点，让它成为原子提交。

0862e0270082.en: The weakness is one moment. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here the coordinator crashes just after deciding to commit and before telling anyone. The participants voted yes, so they are not allowed to abort; they do not know the decision, so they cannot commit. They wait, holding their locks, for thirty-one seconds, until the coordinator recovers and reads its log. No other transaction can touch those rows in the meantime. <bookmark mark='b'/> Three-phase commit adds a round so participants can finish on their own, but it is safe only if the network is synchronous. Real systems do something simpler: they make the coordinator itself a replicated state machine, a Paxos or Raft group, so it never really goes away.
0862e0270082.zh: 弱点在于一个瞬间。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里，协调者在决定提交之后、通知任何人之前崩溃了。参与者们投了赞成票，所以不允许中止；它们又不知道决定是什么，所以也无法提交。它们只能持着锁等待，一等就是三十一秒，直到协调者恢复过来、读出自己的日志。在此期间，其他任何事务都碰不了那些行。<bookmark mark='b'/>三阶段提交多加了一轮，让参与者能够自行收尾，但只有在网络是同步的情况下它才安全。真实的系统做法更简单：把协调者本身做成一个复制状态机，也就是一个 Paxos 或 Raft 组，这样它就永远不会真正消失。

10b1a5acac42.en: Google's Spanner, in 2012, ran transactions across datacenters on several continents and made them linearizable, using clocks. <bookmark mark='a'/> Its TrueTime interface does not return a time; it returns an interval guaranteed to contain the true time, a few milliseconds wide, kept narrow by GPS receivers and atomic clocks in every datacenter. <bookmark mark='b'/> To commit, a coordinator picks as timestamp the latest possible current time, and then waits until the earliest possible current time has passed it, about two epsilon, before releasing locks and reporting success. <bookmark mark='c'/> After that wait, any transaction that starts later in real time is certain to get a larger timestamp, so timestamp order is real-time order. The wait overlaps the Paxos round that replicates the commit, so with an epsilon of one or four milliseconds it costs nothing; with seven it adds six.
10b1a5acac42.zh: 2012年，Google 的 Spanner 在横跨几个大洲的数据中心之间运行事务，并借助时钟让它们可线性化。<bookmark mark='a'/>它的 TrueTime 接口返回的不是一个时间，而是一个保证包含真实时间的区间，只有几毫秒宽，靠每个数据中心里的 GPS 接收器和原子钟把它维持得很窄。<bookmark mark='b'/>提交时，协调者选取当前时间可能的最晚值作为时间戳，然后一直等到当前时间可能的最早值也超过了它，大约两个 epsilon，才释放锁并报告成功。<bookmark mark='c'/>等过这一段之后，任何在真实时间里更晚开始的事务，都必定得到更大的时间戳，所以时间戳的顺序就是真实时间的顺序。这段等待与复制这次提交的 Paxos 轮次相互重叠，所以当 epsilon 是一毫秒或四毫秒时，它没有任何代价；是七毫秒时，会多出六毫秒。

c57eccc3c74f.en: Most of us do not have atomic clocks in every building. <bookmark mark='a'/> We ran four processes whose clocks disagree by up to five milliseconds, sending each other messages that take up to three. Stamped with their physical clocks, one message in five appears to arrive before it was sent. Lamport's clock never gets causality wrong, but its numbers have nothing to do with time: after ten seconds it reads six thousand. <bookmark mark='b'/> Sandeep Kulkarni and his colleagues combined the two in 2014. A hybrid logical clock keeps the largest physical time it has heard of, from its own clock or from any message, plus a small counter to break ties. <bookmark mark='c'/> It never gets causality wrong, it never strays from true time by more than the clocks' own disagreement, and the counter stayed below eight. CockroachDB and MongoDB stamp their transactions this way. Without Spanner's guaranteed bound they cannot simply wait it out, so a read that meets a value within its clock uncertainty restarts at a later timestamp instead.
c57eccc3c74f.zh: 我们大多数人可没法在每栋楼里都放上原子钟。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们运行了四个进程，它们的时钟彼此相差最多五毫秒，互相发送的消息最多要三毫秒才能送达。如果用各自的物理时钟打时间戳，每五条消息里就有一条看起来是在发出之前就到达了。Lamport 时钟从不会把因果关系弄错，但它的数值和时间毫无关系：十秒之后，它显示的是六千。<bookmark mark='b'/>2014年，Sandeep Kulkarni 和他的同事们把两者结合了起来。混合逻辑时钟记住它听说过的最大物理时间，不管来自自己的时钟还是任何一条消息，再加上一个小计数器来打破平局。<bookmark mark='c'/>它从不弄错因果关系，偏离真实时间也从不超过各个时钟本身的分歧，而且计数器始终小于八。CockroachDB 和 MongoDB 就是这样给事务打时间戳的。它们没有 Spanner 那样有保证的误差上界，没法简单地等过去，所以一次读取如果遇到落在自己时钟不确定范围之内的值，就改用一个更晚的时间戳重新开始。

4ad445c4c11e.en: Most systems do not run consensus themselves. <bookmark mark='a'/> They ask a small coordination service, Google's Chubby or Apache ZooKeeper, built on Paxos-like protocols, to hold their locks, elect their leaders and store their configuration. <bookmark mark='b'/> A lock in such a service is really a lease: it expires unless the holder keeps renewing it, so a crashed holder cannot block everyone for ever. <bookmark mark='c'/> But a holder that is merely paused, by a long garbage collection, can wake up after its lease has expired and been granted to someone else, and write, unaware. <bookmark mark='d'/> The fix is a fencing token: every grant carries a number that only increases, and the storage refuses any write carrying a smaller number than one it has already seen.
4ad445c4c11e.zh: 大多数系统并不自己运行共识。<bookmark mark='a'/>它们请一个小型的协调服务，比如 Google 的 Chubby 或 Apache ZooKeeper，这些服务建立在类 Paxos 协议之上，替它们持有锁、选举领导者、保存配置。<bookmark mark='b'/>这类服务里的锁其实是一份租约：除非持有者不断续约，否则它就会过期，所以崩溃了的持有者不会把所有人永远堵住。<bookmark mark='c'/>但一个只是暂停了的持有者，比如卡在一次漫长的垃圾回收里，可能在租约已经过期、又被授予别人之后才醒来，然后毫不知情地写入数据。<bookmark mark='d'/>解决办法是栅栏令牌：每次授予都附带一个只增不减的编号，只要一次写入携带的编号比存储已经见过的某个编号小，存储就拒绝它。

357fabe0f9f4.en: Jeffrey Dean and Sanjay Ghemawat's MapReduce, of 2004, let a programmer write two small functions and run them on thousands of machines. <bookmark mark='a'/> The input, stored in pieces across the cluster, is split, and a map function runs on each split: for the Job, it emits each word with a count of one, combined locally into a count per word. <bookmark mark='b'/> The shuffle sends every word to one reducer, chosen by hashing the word, so all the counts for a word meet in one place. <bookmark mark='c'/> Each reducer adds them up. <bookmark mark='d'/> For the novels: twenty-five megabytes in, six megabytes of partial counts shuffled, fifty-eight thousand distinct words out. The programmer writes none of the distribution, the scheduling or the recovery.
357fabe0f9f4.zh: Jeffrey Dean 和 Sanjay Ghemawat 在2004年提出的 MapReduce，让程序员只需写两个小函数，就能在几千台机器上运行。<bookmark mark='a'/>输入以分块的形式存放在整个集群中，先被切分，然后在每个切片上运行一个 map 函数：对于 那项任务，它为每个单词输出一个计数一，并在本地合并成每个单词的计数。<bookmark mark='b'/>洗牌（shuffle）按单词的哈希值选出一个 reducer，把每个单词都送到那里，于是同一个单词的所有计数都在同一处汇合。<bookmark mark='c'/>每个 reducer 把它们加起来。<bookmark mark='d'/>就那些小说而言：输入二十五兆字节，洗牌传送了六兆字节的部分计数，输出五万八千个不同的单词。分布、调度和恢复，这些程序员一样都不用写。

9849cb9c3065.en: We ran the Job five ways. <bookmark mark='a'/> With nothing going wrong, half a second. With Pebble four crashing at four tenths of a second, six tenths, three finished maps redone, and the same answer. <bookmark mark='b'/> Re-execution is safe because map and reduce are functions: running a task twice gives the same output, and the master simply uses whichever copy it hears about first. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now make Pebble six eight times slower, a straggler, like a machine with a failing disk. With backup tasks the Job takes point five nine seconds; without them, point eight one, a third longer, because everyone waits for the slow machine's last task. Google's paper reported the same effect: a large sort forty-four percent slower with backup tasks turned off.
9849cb9c3065.zh: 我们用五种方式运行了 那项任务。<bookmark mark='a'/>什么都没出错时，用时半秒。让四号 Pebble 在零点四秒时崩溃，用时零点六秒，重做了三个已经完成的 map 任务，答案不变。<bookmark mark='b'/>重新执行之所以安全，是因为 map 和 reduce 都是函数：一个任务运行两次，输出也一样，主节点只需采用它最先听到的那一份。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在让六号 Pebble 慢八倍，成为一个掉队者，就像一台磁盘快要坏掉的机器。有备份任务时，那项任务用时零点五九秒；没有备份任务时，零点八一秒，多出三分之一，因为所有人都在等那台慢机器的最后一个任务。Google 的论文报告了同样的效应：关掉备份任务后，一次大规模排序慢了百分之四十四。

7de510774250.en: How far does it scale? <bookmark mark='a'/> One worker takes three point eight seconds, more than the plain Job, because of the overheads of splitting, scheduling and shuffling. Sixteen workers are seven times faster, not sixteen; sixty-four, barely faster than thirty-two. <bookmark mark='b'/> Every task pays a fixed start-up cost, the shuffle and the reduces do not shrink as mappers are added, and the slowest task sets the finishing time. It is Amdahl's law from Part 10 again, at the scale of a datacenter. MapReduce was built for jobs of terabytes, where these overheads vanish into the work.
7de510774250.zh: 它能扩展到多大规模？<bookmark mark='a'/>一个工作节点要用三点八秒，比普通的 那项任务还慢，因为切分、调度和洗牌都有开销。十六个工作节点快了七倍，而不是十六倍；六十四个，几乎不比三十二个快。<bookmark mark='b'/>每个任务都要付出固定的启动开销，洗牌和 reduce 阶段不会随着 mapper 增多而缩短，而最慢的那个任务决定了完成的时间。这又是第10部分的阿姆达尔定律，只不过换到了数据中心的尺度上。MapReduce 是为太字节级的作业设计的，在那里，这些开销会淹没在工作量里。

6bc2cee963e7.en: The ledger gets row fifteen. <bookmark mark='a'/> The Job as MapReduce on sixteen Pebbles, one of which crashes: six tenths of a second, four and a half times faster than one Pebble, and correct despite the crash. <bookmark mark='b'/> The novels start out spread across the cluster's disks, as Google's file system kept its data. That is the real lesson of row fourteen: move the computation to the data, not the data across an ocean.
6bc2cee963e7.zh: 账本添上第十五行。<bookmark mark='a'/>那项任务以 MapReduce 的方式运行在十六台 Pebble 上，其中一台崩溃了：用时零点六秒，比一台 Pebble 快四点五倍，而且尽管发生了崩溃，结果依然正确。<bookmark mark='b'/>那些小说一开始就分散存放在集群的各个磁盘上，就像 Google 的文件系统存放数据那样。这才是第十四行真正的教训：把计算移到数据那里，而不是把数据搬过一整片大洋。

a7f01f8f508d.en: MapReduce wrote everything to disk between stages, which made long pipelines slow. <bookmark mark='a'/> Matei Zaharia's Spark, in 2012, kept datasets in memory, and handled failure by remembering each dataset's lineage, the chain of transformations that produced it: a lost piece is simply recomputed. <bookmark mark='b'/> Streaming systems run the same model on input that never ends, grouping events into windows by when they happened rather than when they arrived, with watermarks to say that no older events are expected, and a policy for those that arrive anyway. <bookmark mark='c'/> They get exactly-once results by taking Chandy and Lamport's snapshots of every operator, and replaying the input since the last one after a crash. <bookmark mark='d'/> The ideas that last are MapReduce's: deterministic tasks, recovery by re-execution, and computation moved to the data.
a7f01f8f508d.zh: MapReduce 在各个阶段之间把所有东西都写到磁盘上，这让长流水线变得很慢。<bookmark mark='a'/>2012年，Matei Zaharia 的 Spark 把数据集保存在内存里，并通过记住每个数据集的血缘来应对故障，血缘就是产生它的那一串变换：丢失的分块只要重新算一遍就行。<bookmark mark='b'/>流处理系统把同样的模型用在永不结束的输入上，按事件发生的时间、而不是到达的时间把它们归入窗口，用水位线来宣告不会再有更早的事件，并为那些仍然迟到的事件定一套处理策略。<bookmark mark='c'/>它们对每个算子做 Chandy 和 Lamport 的快照，并在崩溃后重放自上一次快照以来的输入，从而得到恰好一次的结果。<bookmark mark='d'/>真正经久不衰的，是 MapReduce 的思想：确定性的任务，靠重新执行来恢复，以及把计算移到数据那里。

581e71248129.en: Chapter seven. The tail at scale.
581e71248129.zh: 第七章。规模下的尾延迟。

748043605c74.en: Jeff Dean and Luiz Barroso's paper of 2013 starts from one observation. A web search, or a social media feed, fans out: one user request becomes requests to a hundred or a thousand servers, and the answer waits for all of them. <bookmark mark='a'/> Suppose each server answers in ten milliseconds, except one request in a hundred, which takes a full second, because of a garbage collection, or a queue behind some large request. <bookmark mark='b'/> With one server, one percent of requests are slow. Waiting for ten, nearly ten percent. Waiting for a hundred, sixty-three percent: one minus point nine nine to the hundred. Our simulation lands on the curve. <bookmark mark='c'/> The rare event at each server is the usual event for the service. Making every server's tail shorter is expensive; the trick is to tolerate it.
748043605c74.zh: Jeff Dean 和 Luiz Barroso 2013年的论文，从一个观察出发。一次网页搜索，或者一条社交媒体信息流，都会扇出：一个用户请求变成发往一百台甚至一千台服务器的请求，而答案要等它们全部回来。<bookmark mark='a'/>假设每台服务器都在十毫秒内应答，只是每一百个请求里有一个例外，要花整整一秒，原因可能是一次垃圾回收，或者排在某个大请求后面的队列里。<bookmark mark='b'/>只有一台服务器时，百分之一的请求是慢的。等十台，将近百分之十。等一百台，百分之六十三：一减去零点九九的一百次方。我们的模拟结果正好落在这条曲线上。<bookmark mark='c'/>每台服务器上的罕见事件，对整个服务来说却是常态。把每台服务器的尾部都缩短，代价高昂；诀窍在于容忍它。

2ae632059d52.en: The simplest remedy is to ask twice. <bookmark mark='a'/> If a server has not answered within thirty milliseconds, about its ninety-fifth percentile, send the same request to another replica and use whichever reply comes first. <bookmark mark='b'/> It costs about five percent more requests. With a fan-out of a hundred, the median falls from a full second to forty-three milliseconds. The ninety-ninth percentile improves too, until the fan-out is so large that some request meets two slow replicas in a row. <bookmark mark='c'/> Google's systems go further with tied requests: send to two servers at once, and whichever starts the work first tells the other to cancel.
2ae632059d52.zh: 最简单的补救办法，是问两次。<bookmark mark='a'/>如果一台服务器在三十毫秒内还没应答，这大约是它的第九十五百分位，就把同一个请求发给另一个副本，谁的回复先到就用谁的。<bookmark mark='b'/>这只多花大约百分之五的请求。在扇出为一百时，中位数从整整一秒降到四十三毫秒。第九十九百分位也会改善，直到扇出大到某个请求接连碰上两个慢副本为止。<bookmark mark='c'/>Google 的系统更进一步，使用绑定请求：同时发给两台服务器，谁先开始干活，就通知另一台取消。

f6618b16acaa.en: Tails also come from uneven load, and one of the best results in randomized algorithms fixes that. <bookmark mark='a'/> Send a thousand requests to a thousand servers at random, and the busiest server gets about five and a half of them, as Part 20's balls-in-bins analysis predicts. Instead, sample two servers and send each request to the less loaded one: the busiest gets three. Exponentially better, for one extra probe. <bookmark mark='b'/> A third choice adds little. Load balancers like NGINX and Envoy ship the power of two choices as their default.
f6618b16acaa.zh: 长尾也来自负载不均，而随机算法中最漂亮的结果之一正好能解决它。<bookmark mark='a'/>把一千个请求随机发给一千台服务器，最忙的那台大约会收到五个半，正如第20部分的球与箱子分析所预测的。换个做法，每次抽样两台服务器，把请求发给负载较轻的那台：最忙的只收到三个。指数级的改进，代价只是多探测一次。<bookmark mark='b'/>第三个选择几乎没有额外的好处。像 NGINX 和 Envoy 这样的负载均衡器，都把双选之力作为默认策略。

0bc74bcb74b4.en: Requests are not balls that land and stay; they wait in queues and leave. Michael Mitzenmacher's supermarket model asks the same question for queues. <bookmark mark='a'/> A hundred servers, requests arriving at random, each taking a random time. Sent to a random server, each server becomes Part 31's single queue, and the tail explodes as load approaches capacity: at ninety-five percent load the ninety-ninth percentile is eighty-two times the service time. <bookmark mark='b'/> Round robin, which never sends two requests in a row to the same server, halves that, and no more, because job lengths still vary. <bookmark mark='c'/> Two random choices, picking the shorter of two queues, brings it to ten and a half: queue lengths now fall off doubly exponentially. <bookmark mark='d'/> Asking every server for its queue length gets five, but asking a hundred servers costs a hundred messages per request. Two choices gets most of the way for two.
0bc74bcb74b4.zh: 请求并不是落下就不动的球；它们在队列里等待，然后离开。Michael Mitzenmacher 的超市模型，就是针对队列提出同样的问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>一百台服务器，请求随机到达，每个请求的处理时间也是随机的。如果随机发给一台服务器，每台服务器就成了第31部分里的单个队列，当负载逼近容量时，尾部会急剧膨胀：在百分之九十五的负载下，第九十九百分位是服务时间的八十二倍。<bookmark mark='b'/>轮询从不把连续两个请求发给同一台服务器，它能把这个数字减半，但也仅此而已，因为作业的长短仍然各不相同。<bookmark mark='c'/>两个随机选择，挑两条队列中较短的那条，能把它降到十点五：队列长度现在呈双指数衰减。<bookmark mark='d'/>询问每一台服务器的队列长度能降到五，可是询问一百台服务器，每个请求要花一百条消息。两个选择只用两条消息，就走完了大部分的路。

c8eefd946de0.en: Real requests pass through chains of services, and the tail travels with them. <bookmark mark='a'/> Give each service a median of ten milliseconds and a ninety-ninth percentile of sixty-five. Through three in a row, the end-to-end ninety-ninth percentile is a hundred and twenty milliseconds, not the hundred and ninety-two you get by adding; through ten, two hundred and sixty-five, not six hundred and fifty. Percentiles do not add, which makes naive latency budgets too generous for chains and, as we saw, far too stingy for fan-outs. <bookmark mark='b'/> Retries multiply. If the bottom service is down and each of three layers retries three times, every user request becomes sixty-four attempts at the bottom, just when it can least afford them: the retry storm of the next chapter, built in. <bookmark mark='c'/> The remedies are boring and effective: send the remaining deadline with every call so that work nobody awaits is never started, retry at one layer only, and cap retries at a tenth of requests, so that even four layers add less than half again.
c8eefd946de0.zh: 真实的请求要穿过一串服务，尾延迟也跟着它们一路传递。<bookmark mark='a'/>假设每个服务的中位数是十毫秒，第九十九百分位是六十五毫秒。连续经过三个服务，端到端的第九十九百分位是一百二十毫秒，而不是相加得到的一百九十二毫秒；经过十个，是两百六十五毫秒，而不是六百五十毫秒。百分位数不能相加，这使得朴素的延迟预算对链式调用过于宽松，而正如我们看到的，对扇出又过于吝啬。<bookmark mark='b'/>重试会成倍放大。如果最底层的服务宕机了，而三层中的每一层都重试三次，那么每个用户请求在最底层都会变成六十四次尝试，而且恰恰发生在它最承受不起的时候：这就是下一章的重试风暴，被预先内置了进去。<bookmark mark='c'/>补救办法朴实而有效：每次调用都带上剩余的截止时间，这样没人在等的工作就永远不会开始；只在一层重试；并把重试的上限定为请求数的十分之一，这样即使有四层，增加的量也不到原来的一半。

c1d0fb45e5fa.zh: 第八章。大规模下的故障。

719821ca1cea.en: At scale, failure stops being an event and becomes a rate. <bookmark mark='a'/> A hundred thousand disks failing at one percent a year means about three every day. Recovery has to be automatic, and so routine that nobody is paged. <bookmark mark='b'/> Worse, failures are not independent. A power unit or a top-of-rack switch takes down many machines at once; a bad configuration pushed everywhere takes down everything. So replicas go in different failure domains, and changes roll out slowly. <bookmark mark='c'/> Gray failures are machines that are slow, or fail only some requests, and still pass their health checks. <bookmark mark='d'/> And metastable failures, named in 2022, are the strangest: the trigger passes, but the system stays down, held there by its own reaction.
719821ca1cea.zh: 到了这样的规模，故障不再是一个事件，而成了一个速率。<bookmark mark='a'/>十万块磁盘，每年的故障率是百分之一，就意味着大约每天坏三块。恢复必须是自动的，而且要平常到不需要呼叫任何人来处理。<bookmark mark='b'/>更糟的是，故障并不相互独立。一个电源单元，或者一台机架顶部交换机，会一下子让许多台机器宕掉；一份推送到所有地方的错误配置，会让一切都宕掉。所以副本要放在不同的故障域里，变更要慢慢地逐步上线。<bookmark mark='c'/>灰色故障，是指那些变慢了、或者只让一部分请求失败的机器，它们仍然能通过健康检查。<bookmark mark='d'/>而亚稳态故障在2022年得到命名，它是最奇怪的一种：触发因素已经过去了，系统却仍然瘫在那里，被它自己的反应困住。

e2be9a1c8f19.en: In 2009 Jeff Dean listed what a typical new Google cluster goes through in its first year. <bookmark mark='a'/> About a thousand individual machine failures and thousands of disk failures. Twenty racks failing, each taking forty to eighty machines with it, and five racks going wonky, losing half their packets. A dozen or so router failures and reloads, a network rewiring, and a power distribution failure that takes down five hundred to a thousand machines for six hours. <bookmark mark='b'/> Do the arithmetic for machines that last three years on average. A six-hour job on a thousand machines finishes without a single failure only four times in five. A day on ten thousand machines, essentially never. <bookmark mark='c'/> So recovery is the normal path, not the exception: MapReduce's re-execution, Raft's elections and Dynamo's hinted handoff are running somewhere every day.
e2be9a1c8f19.zh: 2009年，Jeff Dean 列出了一个典型的 Google 新集群在第一年里会经历的事。<bookmark mark='a'/>大约一千次单台机器故障，以及数千次磁盘故障。二十个机架故障，每次带走四十到八十台机器；还有五个机架出现异常，丢掉一半的数据包。十几次路由器故障和重新加载，一次网络重新布线，以及一次配电故障，让五百到一千台机器停机六个小时。<bookmark mark='b'/>来算一算，假设机器平均能用三年。一个在一千台机器上运行六个小时的作业，五次里只有四次能一次故障都不遇到就完成。在一万台机器上运行一天，基本上不可能。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以恢复是正常路径，而不是例外：MapReduce 的重新执行、Raft 的选举，以及 Dynamo 的提示移交，每天都在某个地方运行着。

961a7c75f83f.en: Availability is measured in nines. Ninety-nine point nine percent, three nines, allows about nine hours of downtime a year. <bookmark mark='a'/> Parts in series multiply. A request that needs ten services, each at three nines, succeeds only ninety-nine percent of the time; a hundred, about ninety percent, more than a month of failure a year. That is why a page that calls many services must tolerate some of them failing. <bookmark mark='b'/> Replicas in parallel multiply the other way: if any one of three independent replicas will do, three nines become nine nines, thirty milliseconds of downtime a year. <bookmark mark='c'/> But the word independent carries the whole result. Put the three replicas in one rack whose switch fails a twentieth of a percent of the time, and they are worse than a single machine elsewhere. In three racks, two million simulated moments saw no outage at all. <bookmark mark='d'/> So never promise more than your dependencies multiply to, shorten the chain of things a request needs, and put replicas in separate failure domains: racks, power feeds, buildings, regions.
961a7c75f83f.zh: 可用性用几个九来衡量。百分之九十九点九，也就是三个九，一年允许大约九个小时的停机。<bookmark mark='a'/>串联的部件，可用性相乘。一个请求需要十个服务，每个都是三个九，那它只有百分之九十九的时间能成功；需要一百个，大约是百分之九十，一年里有一个多月都在失败。这就是为什么一个调用许多服务的页面，必须容忍其中一些服务失败。<bookmark mark='b'/>并联的副本，则朝另一个方向相乘：如果三个独立副本里任何一个都能用，三个九就变成了九个九，一年只有三十毫秒的停机。<bookmark mark='c'/>但“独立”这个词，承载了整个结论。把三个副本放进同一个机架，而这个机架的交换机有百分之零点零五的时间会故障，那它们比放在别处的单独一台机器还要差。放在三个机架里，两百万个模拟时刻，一次停机都没有出现。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以，承诺的可用性，永远不要超过你的各项依赖相乘的结果；缩短一个请求所依赖的链条；把副本放在不同的故障域里：机架、供电线路、楼宇、区域。

fe74e6b53245.en: Every recovery we have seen starts with a decision: this machine has failed. But a machine that has crashed and one that is merely slow look the same from outside. <bookmark mark='a'/> We simulated heartbeats every hundred milliseconds across a network that alternates between calm and congested spells, with occasional garbage-collection pauses. A fixed timeout must be long enough for the worst spell: a timeout of a hundred and seventy-five milliseconds raises about a hundred false alarms an hour, and getting below a few an hour means waiting a quarter of a second or more. <bookmark mark='b'/> The phi accrual detector, used by Cassandra and Akka, instead keeps a window of recent gaps and raises its suspicion as the current silence becomes less likely. It needs no hand-tuned timeout, and it adapts when the network changes. But on our trace it lands on almost the same curve: faster detection buys false alarms, whichever detector you use. <bookmark mark='c'/> Neither can be certain, which is Part 38's lesson again. So a node that has been declared dead must be fenced off, by a new term, an epoch or a fencing token, because it may wake up and keep working.
fe74e6b53245.zh: 我们见过的每一次恢复，都从一个判定开始：这台机器已经失效了。但一台已经崩溃的机器，和一台只是变慢了的机器，从外面看是一样的。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们模拟了每一百毫秒一次的心跳，网络在平静和拥塞两种时段之间交替，偶尔还有垃圾回收造成的停顿。固定的超时必须足够长，长到能熬过最糟的时段：一百七十五毫秒的超时，每小时会产生大约一百次误报；要把误报降到每小时几次以下，就得等上四分之一秒，甚至更久。<bookmark mark='b'/>Cassandra 和 Akka 使用的 phi 累积故障检测器则不同，它保留一个窗口，记录最近的心跳间隔，当前的沉默越不可能出现，它的怀疑就升得越高。它不需要手工调节的超时，而且会在网络变化时自我适应。但在我们的轨迹上，它几乎落在同一条曲线上：无论用哪种检测器，更快的检测都要用误报来换。<bookmark mark='c'/>两者都无法确定，这又是第38部分的教训。所以，一个被宣布死亡的节点必须被隔离出去，用一个新的任期、一个纪元，或者一个隔离令牌，因为它可能会醒过来，继续干活。

98edd4331414.en: Here is a metastable failure, simulated. A server can answer a hundred requests a second and normally gets eighty. Clients give up after one second and retry, up to three times. <bookmark mark='a'/> For ten seconds, load spikes to a hundred and sixty. Without retries the server falls behind, and when the spike passes it slowly drains its queue and recovers. <bookmark mark='b'/> With retries, every slow request comes back as two, three, four requests. The server is now working mostly on requests whose clients have already given up, every answer is too late, and goodput stays at zero long after the spike has gone. Random backoff does not save it. <bookmark mark='c'/> What does is refusing work that can no longer be useful: dropping requests whose deadline has passed brings the server straight back. Load shedding, retry budgets and circuit breakers are the same idea, and part 50 builds them.
98edd4331414.zh: 这是一次模拟的亚稳态故障。一台服务器每秒能应答一百个请求，平时收到八十个。客户端等一秒就放弃并重试，最多重试三次。<bookmark mark='a'/>有十秒钟，负载猛增到一百六十。没有重试的时候，服务器会落后，等峰值过去，它慢慢清空队列，恢复过来。<bookmark mark='b'/>有了重试，每一个慢请求都会变成两个、三个、四个请求再回来。服务器现在主要在处理那些客户端早已放弃的请求，每一个应答都来得太晚，峰值过去很久之后，有效吞吐仍然是零。随机退避也救不了它。<bookmark mark='c'/>能救它的，是拒绝那些已经不可能有用的工作：丢弃已经过了截止时间的请求，服务器立刻就恢复了。负载削减、重试预算和熔断器，都是同一个想法，第50部分会把它们搭建出来。

0143f177cfdd.en: Because failure is constant, the large operators practise it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Netflix's Chaos Monkey, from 2011, kills machines in production, at random, during working hours, so that recovery is exercised every day instead of discovered during a crisis. <bookmark mark='b'/> Companies hold game days that fail an entire datacenter on purpose. <bookmark mark='c'/> And the industry publishes blameless post-mortems of real outages, which show the same causes over and over: a configuration change, a retry storm, an expired certificate, a dependency loop where the recovery tool depends on the thing that failed. <bookmark mark='d'/> It is the lesson of our Raft campaign at datacenter scale: the code that runs only during failures is the least tested code in the system.
0143f177cfdd.zh: 正因为故障无时不在，大型运营者会主动演练它。<bookmark mark='a'/>Netflix 在2011年推出的 Chaos Monkey，会在生产环境中、在工作时间里，随机杀掉机器，这样恢复每天都在被演练，而不是在危机之中才被发现。<bookmark mark='b'/>各家公司会举行演练日，故意让整个数据中心失效。<bookmark mark='c'/>业界还会公开发布真实故障的不追责事后复盘，它们一再显示同样的原因：一次配置变更，一场重试风暴，一张过期的证书，还有一个依赖环，也就是用来恢复的工具，恰恰依赖于那个失效的东西。<bookmark mark='d'/>这正是我们对 Raft 发起的那一轮攻击，放大到数据中心规模的教训：只在故障时才运行的代码，是系统里测试得最少的代码。

9d25a2aab68f.en: Chapter nine. Frontier: how little coordination can we get away with?
9d25a2aab68f.zh: 第九章。前沿：我们最少能用多少协调？

1c541aed019d.en: Every guarantee in this part costs coordination: replicas waiting for each other, across a datacenter or an ocean. So which problems actually need it? <bookmark mark='a'/> Joseph Hellerstein conjectured an answer in 2010, and Tom Ameloot and his colleagues proved it: a problem can be solved consistently without coordination if and only if it is monotonic, meaning new information never retracts an earlier conclusion. <bookmark mark='b'/> Counting likes and adding to a set are monotonic, and our set replicas converged in all thousand runs. Removing from a plain set is not, and converged in only fifteen. Unique usernames and non-negative balances are not monotonic either: some operations must wait. <bookmark mark='c'/> Peter Bailis turned this into an engineering tool, invariant confluence: check each invariant of an application separately. In the standard TPC-C benchmark, most of them need no coordination at all, and a database that knows it can run them many times faster.
1c541aed019d.zh: 这一部分里的每一项保证，都要付出协调的代价：副本彼此等待，跨越一个数据中心，或者一片大洋。那么，哪些问题真正需要协调？<bookmark mark='a'/>Joseph Hellerstein 在2010年猜想了一个答案，Tom Ameloot 和他的同事证明了它：一个问题能够在没有协调的情况下被一致地解决，当且仅当它是单调的，也就是说，新的信息永远不会收回先前的结论。<bookmark mark='b'/>统计点赞数、往集合里添加元素，都是单调的，我们的集合副本在全部一千次运行里都收敛了。从普通集合里删除元素则不是单调的，只在其中十五次运行里收敛了。唯一的用户名和非负的余额，也都不是单调的：有些操作必须等待。<bookmark mark='c'/>Peter Bailis 把这变成了一件工程工具，叫做不变式汇合：分别检查一个应用的每一条不变式。在标准的 TPC-C 基准测试里，大多数不变式根本不需要协调，而一个知道这一点的数据库，可以把它们运行得快很多倍。

82e456202cf9.en: CAP draws one line through the hierarchy of Chapter two: linearizable systems cannot stay available during a partition. <bookmark mark='a'/> But where exactly is the line? In 2011 Prince Mahajan, Lorenzo Alvisi and Mike Dahlin proved that no model stronger than a form of causal consistency can be both always available and convergent. Causality, Lamport's happened-before from Part 38, is the most an always-available system can promise. <bookmark mark='b'/> And it can be had at global scale: systems like COPS and Eiger give causal consistency across datacenters, even with transactions. <bookmark mark='c'/> What remains open is its price: how much metadata each write must carry to track causality among millions of clients. The lower bounds and the best systems are still far apart.
82e456202cf9.zh: CAP 在第二章的层级结构里画了一条线：可线性化的系统，在网络分区期间无法保持可用。<bookmark mark='a'/>但这条线究竟在哪里？2011年，Prince Mahajan、Lorenzo Alvisi 和 Mike Dahlin 证明了：没有任何比某种形式的因果一致性更强的模型，能够既始终可用、又收敛。因果性，也就是第38部分里 Lamport 的“先发生于”关系，是一个始终可用的系统所能承诺的极限。<bookmark mark='b'/>而且它可以在全球规模上实现：像 COPS 和 Eiger 这样的系统，能在多个数据中心之间提供因果一致性，甚至支持事务。<bookmark mark='c'/>悬而未决的是它的代价：每一次写入必须携带多少元数据，才能在数百万个客户端之间追踪因果关系。下界和最好的系统之间，仍然相距甚远。

08619963a8f2.en: How would you know whether a database actually delivers what it promises? Watch only what clients saw, and look for a contradiction. In general this is hard: deciding whether a history is linearizable, or serializable, is NP-complete. <bookmark mark='a'/> Kyle Kingsbury and Peter Alvaro's Elle, in 2020, makes it easy by choosing the test. Every transaction appends unique numbers to lists and reads whole lists, so every read reveals exactly which writes came before it, and in what order. <bookmark mark='b'/> From that, Elle draws an edge whenever one transaction must have come before another. Here transaction three sixty appended three fifty to key four, and three sixty-two appended three fifty-one right after it, so three sixty came first. But three sixty-two had read key four without three fifty, so it came first. A cycle: no serial order explains what the clients saw. <bookmark mark='c'/> We ran two thousand transactions on two stores. On a single serial copy, no cycles. On a store that reads from a lagging replica, a hundred and forty-three of them, involving eight hundred and thirty-five transactions. Elle has found anomalies like these in a long list of production databases.
08619963a8f2.zh: 你怎么知道一个数据库是否真的兑现了它的承诺？只看客户端看到了什么，然后寻找矛盾。一般来说，这很难：判定一段历史是否可线性化，或者是否可串行化，是 NP 完全的。<bookmark mark='a'/>Kyle Kingsbury 和 Peter Alvaro 在2020年提出的 Elle，通过选择测试的方式，让它变得容易。每个事务都把唯一的数字追加到列表上，并读取整个列表，所以每一次读取都会准确地揭示，哪些写入发生在它之前，以及按什么顺序。<bookmark mark='b'/>由此，每当一个事务必然发生在另一个之前，Elle 就画一条边。这里，事务三百六十把三百五十追加到了键四上，而事务三百六十二紧接着把三百五十一追加了上去，所以三百六十在前。但三百六十二读取键四时，没有看到三百五十，所以三百六十二在前。这是一个环：没有任何串行顺序能解释客户端看到的东西。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们在两个存储上运行了两千个事务。在单一的串行副本上，没有环。在一个从滞后副本读取的存储上，出现了一百四十三个环，涉及八百三十五个事务。Elle 已经在一长串生产数据库里，发现了这样的异常。

5e26cbb440c9.en: Where the field stands. <bookmark mark='a'/> Programming languages such as Bloom and Hydro try to find the monotonic parts of a program automatically, and to insert coordination only where the CALM theorem says it is unavoidable. <bookmark mark='b'/> Sequence CRDTs for collaborative text still struggle to avoid interleaving anomalies with bounded metadata, which matters for local-first software, where your data lives on your devices first. <bookmark mark='c'/> Metastable failures are found after they happen; predicting which systems have a stable bad state, and how big a trigger tips them over, is open. <bookmark mark='d'/> And hedging, retries and admission control interact in ways that have very little theory. <bookmark mark='e'/> This part's research problem sits right there: design a retry policy for our simulator that provably recovers from any finite spike, while keeping the tail benefit that hedging gave us.
5e26cbb440c9.zh: 这个领域目前的状况。<bookmark mark='a'/>Bloom 和 Hydro 这样的编程语言，试图自动找出程序中单调的部分，只在 CALM 定理说无法避免的地方才插入协调。<bookmark mark='b'/>用于协作文本的序列 CRDT，仍然难以在元数据有界的前提下避免交错异常，而这对本地优先软件很重要，在那里，你的数据首先存放在你自己的设备上。<bookmark mark='c'/>亚稳态故障都是在发生之后才被发现的；预测哪些系统存在一个稳定的坏状态，以及多大的触发因素会把它们推过临界点，仍是未解的问题。<bookmark mark='d'/>而对冲、重试和准入控制之间的相互作用，几乎没有什么理论。<bookmark mark='e'/>这一部分的研究题就落在这里：为我们的模拟器设计一种重试策略，可证明地能从任何有限的峰值中恢复，同时保留对冲为我们带来的尾延迟收益。

b5cb79e0addf.en: What we built in this part. The datacenter as one computer, and what its distances cost. Replicas, their lag, and quorums whose overlap buys fresh reads, with the staleness of sloppier quorums measured. The hierarchy of consistency models, CAP stated precisely, and CRDTs, whose merges cannot conflict. A hash ring that moves almost no keys, and Chord's fingers. Two-phase commit, which can block for ever, and Spanner, which waits out its clock uncertainty. The Job as MapReduce on sixteen Pebbles, surviving a crash. And the tail: one slow server in a hundred, hedged requests, two choices, and failures that feed themselves.
b5cb79e0addf.zh: 这一部分我们搭建了什么。把数据中心当作一台计算机，以及它的距离带来的代价。副本、副本的滞后，还有法定人数，它们的重叠换来了新鲜的读取；我们还测量了更宽松的法定人数会有多陈旧。一致性模型的层级，精确表述的 CAP，以及 CRDT，它们的合并不可能冲突。一个几乎不移动任何键的哈希环，以及 Chord 的 finger 表。两阶段提交，它可能永远阻塞；还有 Spanner，它会等过自己时钟的不确定区间。那项任务以 MapReduce 的形式在十六台 Pebble 上运行，并在一次崩溃中存活下来。还有尾延迟：一百台服务器里有一台慢，对冲请求，两次随机选择，以及会自我喂养的故障。

cedc7ff8bcf2.en: Where this comes back. CRDTs return in version control and in local-first web apps, Parts 41 and 42. The tail returns as latency budgets across a graph of services and in search engines. Part 46 builds streams with watermarks and exactly-once state, and query engines that shuffle like MapReduce. Parts 48 and 49 design real systems with sharding, hot keys and fencing tokens. And Part 50 keeps them running, with the load shedding and retry budgets that cure metastable failures.
cedc7ff8bcf2.zh: 它们会在哪里再出现。CRDT 会在版本控制和本地优先的网页应用里回来，也就是第41和第42部分。尾延迟会作为跨越一张服务图的延迟预算回来，也会在搜索引擎里回来。第46部分会搭建带水位线和恰好一次状态的流处理，以及像 MapReduce 一样做洗牌的查询引擎。第48和第49部分会用分片、热点键和隔离令牌来设计真实的系统。而第50部分会让它们持续运行，用的是能治愈亚稳态故障的负载削减和重试预算。

069d2e2930fc.en: In practice. Treat consistency as a product decision: which anomalies may a user see? Start strong and relax only where you have measured the cost. Cassandra and DynamoDB use quorums; Spanner and CockroachDB use consensus and clocks; Redis Cluster splits keys into hash slots. Spark, Flink and Beam are MapReduce's model with memory and watermarks. Watch the ninety-ninth percentile, not the mean, hedge reads that are safe to repeat, and let the load balancer use two choices. And give every request a deadline: back off with jitter, budget your retries, and throw away work nobody is waiting for.
069d2e2930fc.zh: 在实践中。把一致性当作一个产品决策：用户可以看到哪些异常？从强一致开始，只在测量过代价的地方放宽。Cassandra 和 DynamoDB 使用法定人数；Spanner 和 CockroachDB 使用共识和时钟；Redis Cluster 把键划分到哈希槽里。Spark、Flink 和 Beam，是 MapReduce 的模型，再加上内存和水位线。盯住第九十九百分位数，而不是平均值；对可以安全重复的读取做对冲；让负载均衡器使用两次随机选择。还有，给每个请求一个截止时间：带抖动地退避，为重试设定预算，并扔掉没有人在等的工作。

aa48594aa83a.en: Six problems, with full solutions in the part's notes. Pause on any of them. The fifth is a build problem: our MapReduce survives any worker's crash, but not its master's. Make it survive that too, and show that the answer does not change. The last, marked with a star, is a research problem: a retry policy that provably recovers from any finite spike, without giving up what hedging bought.
aa48594aa83a.zh: 六道习题，完整解答在这一部分的笔记里。任何一道都可以暂停来看。第五道是动手题：我们的 MapReduce 能在任何一个工作节点崩溃后存活下来，但它的主节点崩溃时不行。让它在那种情况下也能存活，并证明答案不会改变。最后一道标着星号，是研究题：一种可证明地能从任何有限峰值中恢复的重试策略，同时不放弃对冲带来的好处。

896b5ba6364c.en: That ends Act Seven, Many Machines. Next time, Part 40 opens Act Eight, Building Software, with software engineering: Parnas' information hiding, contracts and subtyping, testing and flaky tests, Brooks' and Conway's laws, and the dependency graph of the very repository that built this series, measured.
896b5ba6364c.zh: 第七幕“众多机器”到此结束。下一次，第40部分将开启第八幕“构建软件”，从软件工程讲起：Parnas 的信息隐藏，契约与子类型，测试与不稳定的测试，Brooks 定律和 Conway 定律，还有构建了这个系列的这个代码仓库本身的依赖图，我们会把它测量出来。

9bd24692775d.en: The books and papers this part follows are on screen and in the notes. Thank you for watching.
9bd24692775d.zh: 这一部分所依据的书和论文都在屏幕上和笔记里。感谢观看。
